review.finding: already_recorded() only catches (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) around json.loads(); a syntactically-valid but structurally-wrong reviews.json (e.g. 'reviews'/'gates' holding a non-dict value, or the document not being an object) raises an uncaught AttributeError from record.get(section)/.get(review_type), propagating unhandled through main() and violating the module's own documented 'never blocks the subagent' guarantee that every other failure path is defensively guarded and tested for.
review.suggestion: Wrap the section-lookup loop (or the whole function body) in a broad try/except that treats any TypeError/AttributeError the same as a parse failure — 'not recorded', salvage still runs — matching the docstring's own promise and the handling already given to this exact class of corruption in handoff_iterate.py's ReviewRecordError path.

review.finding: already_recorded() checks the legacy 'gates' section for every review_type (spec/code/doubt), but the SSoT it deliberately can't import (lib.review_record_legacy.read_sections) restricts 'gates' lookups to review_type in LEGACY_GATE_TYPES ('spec' only). Harmless today, but it's a hand-rolled reimplementation that has already silently drifted from the precedence rule it was modeled on.
review.suggestion: Guard the gates-section check with `if review_type == "spec"` to keep the duplicated logic honestly mirroring read_sections().

review.finding: render_iterate_progress() has grown to ~155 lines of body covering several largely-independent computations (spec/run_id/complexity resolution, mini-plan fallback, external-review-marker lookup, review-cascade status, output assembly). Coherent and well-commented, not blocking, but a future touch would benefit from extracting the review-cascade block into its own helper for independent testability.
review.suggestion: Non-blocking: factor the review-cascade status computation (lines ~126-150) into a small `_resolve_review_cascade_status(project_root, run_id)` helper on a future touch.
